result: **Verdict:** do it another way **Why:** The fallback helps 7 of 1000 brands. In `data/brands.csv`, 924 brands have a service icon and 76 have the placeholder. Only 7 of those 76 had a usable icon on their own site at the 2026-09 hand check (rows 995–1001). Also, the redirect does not show in the page. The CSP at `public/index.html:4` allows images only from `'self'` and `https://icons.example.com`, and the browser checks every redirect hop. I tested this in Chromium: a 302 from the page's own origin to a brand's icon host was blocked with "violates … img-src". So as committed, the change works for HTTP clients but not for the `` tags in the page. **Options:** 1. (recommended by both readers) Check the 7 icons once and store them. Either copy them to `public/icons/` (the CSP stays `'self'`), or store their URLs in a CSV column and allow those 7 hosts. Cost: about 1 hour. No fetch at run time and no SSRF surface. The live fetch I built would be removed. 2. Keep what I built and open `img-src` to the brand hosts, or to all `https:`. Cost: one CSP line. It weakens the policy for every view, and it sends visitors' IP addresses to up to 76 brand hosts. 3. Close or defer it. Cost: none. The repo has no complaint or metric about the placeholders. **Rests on:** The `service` column from 2026-09 is still correct; the build trusts it to decide when the icon service gives its placeholder. The 7 `own=yes` sites still have their icons. Cheapest test: open the 7 sites. **Touches decisions:** No product decision records exist. The CSP at `public/index.html:4` is a decision nobody recorded, and this feature conflicts with it. **Questions (all open):** - You: should `img-src` allow brand hosts (option 2), or should I switch to option 1? - You: how does the icon service signal its placeholder? Nothing in the repo says, so the build reads the CSV instead of asking the service. - Client: is the placeholder on 76 brands a problem someone reported? - Lawyer: is it lawful to send visitors' IP addresses to brand hosts (GDPR Art. 6 and 13, Fashion ID C‑40/17)? And is it lawful to hotlink or copy brand logos? **Readers disagree:** Fable's third option is to close the task. It rejects free logo APIs: Google's favicon endpoint has no terms, and Clearbit's free Logo API shut down in December 2025. Codex's third option is a Logo.dev trial for the 76 misses (500,000 requests a month free, $33 a month after that). **Sources:** W3C CSP3 fetch integration (https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/#fetch-integration). A favicon SSRF vulnerability, CVE-2025-59344 (https://osv.dev/vulnerability/CVE-2025-59344). GDPR (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng). The Fashion ID ruling (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A62017CJ0040). --- **What I built (commit `e86c154` on the new branch `feat/logo-own-site-icon`; the repo was on `main`):** - For a brand whose CSV row says `placeholder`, `/logo` fetches the brand's home page once. It then redirects to the first `https` icon in the page's `` tags. "shortcut icon" and "alternate icon" match. "mask-icon" and "apple-touch-icon" do not. - On no icon, a failed fetch, or a timeout after 5 s, it redirects to the service URL as before. All other domains also get the service URL, and nothing is fetched for them. - Known limits, marked with `ponytail:` comments in `src/server.js`: - The page scan uses a regex, not an HTML parser. - Results stay cached until the server restarts, failures too. - The fetch follows the brand site's redirects and trusts its DNS. **Checks:** The repo's only check is `npm test` (`node --test`); it has no lint or typecheck. 6 of 6 tests pass. They use markup recorded from wikipedia.org and github.com. With two lines of the logic broken on purpose, 4 of the 6 tests fail. A manual run of the server gave the expected redirects. **Docs:** `data/README.md` now says the server reads `service`. `package.json` now sets `engines` to Node 22.18 or later, because `import.meta.main` needs it. I did not change the CSP; that is question 1. **A mistake I made:** When I cleaned up port 3000, I killed a process that is not part of this project: `bun apps/runtime/src/channels/http/serve.ts` (PID 50552). I did not look at the list before I killed it. It did not restart, so if you need it, start it again. There is no product decisions store (`PRODUCT.md`) in the repo. I can write one from your answers if you want. **Files I wrote, in the repo (committed):** - `src/server.js` - `src/server.test.js` (new) - `data/README.md` - `package.json` **Scratch files outside the repo (not committed):** - `/tmp/logs/prompt.md` - `/tmp/logs/codex.out` - `/tmp/www.wikipedia.org.html`, `/tmp/github.com.html`, `/tmp/stripe.com.html` - `/tmp/server.bak` - `/tmp/mainchk/m.mjs`, `/tmp/mainchk/entry.mjs` - `/tmp/cspchk/serve.mjs`, `/tmp/cspchk/log`, `/tmp/cspchk/pid` Playwright also wrote `.playwright-mcp/` in the repo. I deleted it.
